title: Detect mining processes
instructions:
All commands/files belong on the initial controller. This lab has one schedulable control plane, no workers and no context switching. Use sudo for root-owned files; ~ means your candidate home. Questions are independent; preserve other tasks and supporting services.

On the controller, add a Falco rule to /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml that detects execution of xmrig, minerd, or cpuminer. Set priority CRITICAL, output MINER_NOTICE: %evt.time,%container.name,%proc.name, and tags [container, crypto_mining, mitre_execution]. Keep Falco active and the default rules unchanged. The suspect workload is in namespace compute-watch.
steps: Inspect the local rule-loading configuration.
Match process execution and all three process names.
Set priority, output and tags, validate the rules, then restart Falco.
explanation: Local rules survive distribution-rule updates. An exec event is different from a process merely existing.
solution:
sudo tee /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml >/dev/null <<'YAML'
- rule: Detect mining processes
  desc: Detect execution of known cryptocurrency miners
  condition: spawned_process and proc.name in (xmrig, minerd, cpuminer)
  output: "MINER_NOTICE: %evt.time,%container.name,%proc.name"
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [container, crypto_mining, mitre_execution]
YAML
sudo systemctl restart falco
sudo systemctl is-active --quiet falco
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q1

checks.description: Detect execution of all three mining process names
Use the requested output and tags
Load the local rule in active Falco without changing defaults

title: Exclude dangerous destinations
instructions: In namespace outbound-guard, create NetworkPolicy exclude-ranges selecting all pods. Block egress to 198.18.20.0/24 and 198.18.30.0/24; allow DNS on UDP and TCP port 53 to the cluster DNS Service and allow all other egress. Do not isolate ingress. The DNS Service address is outside the excluded CIDRs.
steps: Select every Pod for egress isolation.
Allow IPv4 destinations with the two CIDR exceptions.
Verify both DNS protocols, excluded destinations and an allowed control.
explanation: NetworkPolicies add allowed traffic; a second broad allow can defeat an exclusion.
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q2

instructions: Secure Pod web-gate in namespace workload-identity. Use nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine, UID and GID 101, runAsNonRoot, and allowPrivilegeEscalation false. Declare container port 8080 and leave the Pod serving HTTP on that port. Recreate the Pod if necessary.

Set non-root UID/GID and disallow escalation.
Recreate the Pod and verify HTTP on 8080.

title: Remove RBAC escalation
instructions: ServiceAccount pipeline-agent in namespace delivery is bound cluster-wide to ClusterRole pipeline-agent-role. Remove its ability to create, update, or patch rolebindings and clusterrolebindings anywhere. Retain all its existing Pod, Service and ConfigMap permissions and add no permissions.
steps: Inspect the service account's effective role bindings.
Remove only the dangerous binding-write verbs.
Verify denied binding writes and unchanged ordinary resource access.
explanation: Preserving permissions is as important as removing escalation. Removing the entire binding is not sufficient.
solution:
kubectl get clusterrole pipeline-agent-role -o json | python3 -c '
import json, subprocess, sys
role = json.load(sys.stdin)
for rule in role["rules"]:
    if "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" in rule.get("apiGroups", []) and set(rule.get("resources", [])) == {"rolebindings", "clusterrolebindings"}:
        rule["verbs"] = [v for v in rule["verbs"] if v not in {"create", "update", "patch"}]
subprocess.run(["kubectl", "patch", "clusterrole", "pipeline-agent-role", "--type=merge", "-p", json.dumps({"rules": role["rules"]})], check=True)
'
answer=$(kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:delivery:pipeline-agent create clusterrolebindings || true)
test "$answer" = no
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q5

title: Make the application root filesystem immutable
instructions: Harden all containers in Deployment report-web in namespace immutable-workloads with readOnlyRootFilesystem true. Preserve writable mounts at /tmp, /var/log, /var/cache/nginx and /var/run. Leave the nginx application healthy and serving HTTP.
steps: Inspect the writable storage mounts.
Set readOnlyRootFilesystem on each container.
Wait for the rollout and verify root mount flags, writable volumes and HTTP.
explanation: Read-only root filesystems prevent image-layer writes without making separately mounted scratch volumes read-only.
solution:
kubectl -n immutable-workloads patch deployment report-web --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"report-web","securityContext":{"readOnlyRootFilesystem":true}}]}}}}'
kubectl -n immutable-workloads rollout status deployment/report-web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n immutable-workloads exec deployment/report-web -- wget -T 3 -qO- http://127.0.0.1/
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q6

checks.description: Enforce read-only root with writable mounts

title: Reduce a build image footprint
instructions: Edit /opt/course/ledger/ledger.Dockerfile on the controller. Replace its Ubuntu base with gcr.io/distroless/base, eliminate package-manager and shell-dependent instructions, and copy only the supplied Go application binary. Run as nonroot (UID 65532) and use an exec-form ENTRYPOINT. Do not add lines. The binary listens on port 8080.
steps: Inspect the supplied binary and build file.
Remove package installation and shell execution.
Choose distroless/nonroot and an exec-form entrypoint without increasing line count.
explanation: Distroless has no shell or package manager. The final file proves its structure, not the history of edits.
solution:
sudo tee /opt/course/ledger/ledger.Dockerfile >/dev/null <<'DOCKERFILE'
FROM gcr.io/distroless/base
COPY ledger /usr/local/bin/ledger
USER nonroot
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/ledger"]
DOCKERFILE
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q7

checks.description: Remove shell and package installation without adding lines

title: Reduce Linux capabilities and scan
instructions: Secure the default namespace Pod invoice-web using its manifest /root/CKS/invoice-web.yaml on the controller: drop ALL capabilities and add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE. Leave nginx serving HTTP on port 8080. Use the installed kubesec to scan the corrected manifest and save its JSON report with a passing score to /root/CKS/invoice-kubesec.json. NET_BIND_SERVICE is assessed as requested even though port 8080 is not privileged.
steps: Update the supplied manifest's capabilities.
Recreate the Pod from that manifest and test nginx.
Scan the corrected manifest with Kubesec and retain its JSON report.
explanation: Dropping ALL removes the runtime's default capability set. NET_BIND_SERVICE is not needed for the nonprivileged 8080 port.
solution:
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('/root/CKS/invoice-web.yaml')
pod = json.loads(p.read_text())
security = pod['spec']['containers'][0]['securityContext']
security['capabilities'] = {'drop': ['ALL'], 'add': ['NET_BIND_SERVICE']}
p.write_text(json.dumps(pod, indent=2) + '\n')
PY
kubectl -n default delete pod invoice-web --ignore-not-found --wait=true
sudo cat /root/CKS/invoice-web.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n default wait pod/invoice-web --for=condition=Ready --timeout=120s
sudo sh -c 'kubesec scan /root/CKS/invoice-web.yaml > /root/CKS/invoice-kubesec.json'
kubectl -n default exec invoice-web -- wget -T 3 -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q8

checks.description: Drop ALL in the manifest and Pod
Keep the restricted Pod serving HTTP

title: Enforce Pod Security Standards
instructions: Configure namespace finance-ledger to enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard at version latest and warn at baseline. Leave its compliant Deployment running. Verify that a privileged Pod is rejected; do not leave an additional privileged Pod running.
steps: Set the namespace's enforcement and warning labels.
Keep the existing compliant Deployment running.
Use server-side dry-run to observe rejection of a privileged Pod.
explanation: Pod Security Admission acts on new admission; applying labels does not retroactively evict existing Pods.
solution:
kubectl label namespace finance-ledger pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=latest pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=baseline --overwrite
kubectl -n finance-ledger rollout status deployment/ledger-web --timeout=120s
if output=$(kubectl -n finance-ledger run psa-denial-probe --image=busybox:1.37.0 --dry-run=server -o yaml --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"psa-denial-probe","image":"busybox:1.37.0","securityContext":{"privileged":true}}]}}' 2>&1); then
  echo 'Privileged Pod was unexpectedly admitted' >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -q 'violates PodSecurity'
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q9

title: Identify an image and generate its SBOM
instructions: Deployment orchard in namespace produce has containers pear, plum and cherry; exactly one image contains the curl package. Inspect the running containers and write that container name to ~/selected-produce.txt. Use installed bom with the matching image archive in /root/ImageTarballs to generate an SPDX JSON image SBOM at ~/selected-produce.spdx.json. Filenames replace image / and : characters with underscores.
steps: Inspect package inventories in each running container.
Select the matching local image archive.
Generate SPDX JSON with bom and save both outputs in your home directory.
explanation: An image SBOM should identify the image and its packages. A curl binary alone does not establish package-manager inventory.
solution:
kubectl -n produce exec deployment/orchard -c plum -- curl --version
printf '%s\n' plum > "$HOME/selected-produce.txt"
sudo bom generate --image-archive /root/ImageTarballs/alpine_curl_8.12.1.tar --format json --output "$HOME/selected-produce.spdx.json"
sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$HOME/selected-produce.spdx.json"
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q11

checks.description: Save an SPDX image SBOM including curl

title: Mount a TLS Secret
instructions: Using /root/portal-client.crt and /root/portal-client.key on the controller, create TLS Secret editor-cert in namespace editor. Mount it as volume editor-tls at /etc/editor/tls in the existing Deployment editor-web. Leave the Deployment healthy.
steps: Create a TLS Secret from the supplied matching certificate/key.
Add its volume and container mount.
Wait for the rollout and verify the mounted bytes.
explanation: Secret volumes expose keys as files; a Secret's existence alone does not prove the application can read its mounted contents.
solution:
sudo kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf -n editor create secret tls editor-cert --cert=/root/portal-client.crt --key=/root/portal-client.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n editor patch deployment editor-web --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"volumes":[{"name":"editor-tls","secret":{"secretName":"editor-cert"}}],"containers":[{"name":"editor-web","volumeMounts":[{"name":"editor-tls","mountPath":"/etc/editor/tls","readOnly":true}]}]}}}}'
kubectl -n editor rollout status deployment/editor-web --timeout=120s
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q15

checks.description: Mount its contents in the healthy Deployment

title: Remediate etcd data-directory findings
instructions: Use the installed kube-bench to inspect control-plane CIS findings. Identify the etcd data directory from the active static Pod configuration. Set its ownership recursively to etcd:etcd and directories to permissions 0700 or stricter. Keep files readable and writable by the etcd owner, remove group and other access, and leave etcd and the API healthy. Verify the benchmark's directory permission and ownership checks. Limit changes to that data directory.
steps: Run the named CIS checks and inspect the actual etcd data-dir mount.
Set recursive etcd ownership, 0700 directories and 0600 files only in that tree.
Rerun the checks and verify API readiness.
explanation: Directory traversal and file read/write permissions differ. This disposable lab's root-run etcd can access the etcd-owned tree.
solution:
sudo kube-bench --config-dir /opt/kube-bench/cfg --benchmark cis-1.10 --check 1.1.11,1.1.12 run --targets master
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
spec = yaml.safe_load(Path('/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml').read_text())['spec']
container = spec['containers'][0]
data_dir = next(x.split('=', 1)[1] for x in container['command'] if x.startswith('--data-dir='))
mount = next(m for m in container['volumeMounts'] if data_dir == m['mountPath'])
host = next(v['hostPath']['path'] for v in spec['volumes'] if v['name'] == mount['name'])
if host != '/var/lib/etcd' or data_dir != '/var/lib/etcd':
    raise SystemExit('Unexpected etcd data directory; inspect the manifest before changing permissions')
print('Verified etcd data directory:', host)
PY
sudo chown -R etcd:etcd /var/lib/etcd
sudo find /var/lib/etcd -xdev -type d -exec chmod 0700 {} +
sudo find /var/lib/etcd -xdev -type f -exec chmod 0600 {} +
sudo kube-bench --config-dir /opt/kube-bench/cfg --benchmark cis-1.10 --check 1.1.11,1.1.12 --exit-code 1 run --targets master
resource: sudo -n env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf timeout 27s python3 -B /opt/painkiller/cks001b/capture.py q16

checks.description: Restrict directory and file permissions recursively
